layout_summary: A minimalist movie-poster parody layout on a pure white background, pairing a tall vertical visual on the left (a red stiletto shoe with a pitchfork heel dipping into an overflowing jar of spread) with a stacked serif title lockup on the middle-right. A single-line red sans-serif tagline spans the bottom width to anchor the composition.

alignment_axes: DEVIL (x=46.5%) and BISCOFF (x=46.0%) share a vertical left alignment axis at ~46% and a right edge at ~90%
Bottom tagline is horizontally centered on the canvas (x=7.0% to 93.0%, center x=50.0%)
whitespace: 10% horizontal gutter between the right edge of the shoe/jar scene (x=36.0%) and the title lockup (x=46.0%)
30.5% open white space above the title lockup on the right half
37% vertical empty space between the bottom of BISCOFF (y=55.5%) and the bottom tagline (y=92.5%)
10% vertical gap between the bottom of the jar drip (y=82.5%) and the bottom tagline (y=92.5%)

scene.subject: A glossy red high-heeled stiletto shoe entering from the left edge, whose heel terminates in a three-pronged red pitchfork dipping into an open glass jar of smooth caramelized brown spread, with thick spread overflowing and dripping down the right side of the jar.
scene.composition: Tall vertical composite anchored on the left third; the shoe bleeds off the left canvas edge at y=42%-52% while its pointed toe rises to y=10%, and the jar sits upright beneath the heel from y=55.5% to y=82.5%.
scene.camera: Eye-level studio product shot, crisp focus front-to-back with deep depth of field.
scene.lighting: Bright, clean studio lighting from the right and front-right, creating sharp white specular highlights on the red patent shoe and glossy brown spread, with a soft contact shadow cast to the left of the jar base.

elements.text: Don't be silly Andrea, everybody wants this.

ornaments.description: Pointed devil-tail arrow tip extending upward and right from the top-right serif of the letter 'V' in 'DEVIL'

why_it_works: Instant cultural recognition: faithfully replicates the iconic 'The Devil Wears Prada' poster grid, typography, and red-on-white minimalism.
Clever visual integration seamlessly connects the pitchfork stiletto heel directly into the overflowing jar of spread.
Generous white space isolates the two focal points so the visual punchline and headline read effortlessly in under two seconds.
